Hania Khaled

AI engineer and data scientist - Zewail City 2026

Fresh graduate of the Data Science and Artificial Intelligence program at Zewail City of Science and Technology, working across machine learning, NLP and computer vision. Here are the projects, programs and coursework behind the headline.

Graduation day at the University of Science and Technology at Zewail City, 2026.

Selected work

Featured projects

1

Graduation project - team of 4 - Fall 2025 to Spring 2026

Smart Attendance System Using Face Recognition

Approach
OpenCV (Haar Cascade) face detection and cropping, CNN (ResNet) facial-embedding recognition, presence-duration tracking, live instructor dashboard
Supervisor
Dr. Mohamed Ghalwash
My fall-semester work
Data collection and preparation, Haar Cascade face cropping, building the training dataset

Classroom attendance from one photo per minute instead of a roll call: faces are detected and recognized across frames, and attendance is measured by how long each student is actually present, then shown to instructors on a live dashboard. Designed in the fall semester and implemented the following spring as a two-semester graduation project.

2

LLM safety - Large Language Models course

Goldilocks Defensive AI Agent

Design
Two-stage pipeline: interceptor classifies each prompt, responder answers, refuses, or gives a safe high-level explanation
Rule set
An explicit written constitution both stages follow
Evaluation
Scored 95/100 on the course gauntlet of safe prompts, jailbreak attempts, and ambiguous edge cases

A defensive LLM agent that answers benign prompts helpfully, refuses clearly malicious ones, and responds to ambiguous intent with a safe, non-actionable explanation - with every decision recorded for review.

3

Generative AI course

Generative Models: Autoencoders, VAEs and PCA

Models
Autoencoders and variational autoencoders, trained on medical MNIST, Physarum, MNIST and Fashion-MNIST data
From scratch
PCA implemented in NumPy, plus latent-space analysis of trained VAEs
Frameworks
TensorFlow/Keras and NumPy, developed on Google Colab

A set of representation-learning and generative-modeling notebooks with written reports: training runs, reconstruction results, and exploration of what the latent space learns.

4

Computer vision course

Object Detection and Tracking: YOLO Comparison

System
Person detection and tracking in video with YOLOv8 and DeepSORT, frame by frame
Measured
Three YOLO variants (v10n, v11n, v12n) timed on a 942-frame video: 5.18, 5.23 and 4.72 FPS
Supporting labs
SIFT keypoint matching and Fourier-domain filtering with OpenCV

Detection and multi-object tracking coursework with a full written report, plus a measured speed comparison across three YOLO generations on the same footage.

5

Data visualization coursework - DSAI 203

Interactive Sales and Customer Dashboard

Brief
Designed for a retail-manager client persona, from raw company sales CSV data
Dashboards
Exploratory Tableau dashboard, plus an interactive web implementation with amCharts
Charts
Sales revenue by branch, product-category mix, customer-satisfaction radar, quantity sold over time - with tooltips and range sliders

End-to-end visualization work: a written design phase (client, questions, chart choices with justification), then the implemented dashboard answering sales, product, satisfaction and trend questions.

6

Statistical inference course - R

Diabetes Risk Factor Analysis

Analysis
Diabetic vs non-diabetic group comparisons across glucose, age, blood pressure, BMI, pregnancies and pedigree function
Correlation
Scatter and trend analysis, including glucose vs BMI and glucose vs age
Sampling study
Repeated random samples showing how confidence-interval width shrinks as sample size grows
Toolkit
R with dplyr, ggplot2 and readr

A full statistical-inference project on a patient dataset: hypothesis-driven visual comparisons between diabetic and non-diabetic groups, followed by a sampling experiment on confidence-interval accuracy.

About the graduation projectSmart Attendance was a four-person team project; the approach above is the system the team built, and the named part is my own verified contribution from the fall-semester report.

Depth

Coursework

Course repositories are being published to GitHub progressively - each one passes a content review first. They span data structures, databases, computer networks, software engineering, machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, reinforcement learning, nature-inspired computation, information theory, statistical inference, and the mathematics core of the program.
